name: Stratum Executive Poplin
description:
A dress shirt engineered for the Tier 4 corporate environment: crisp white poplin weave with a subtle self-stripe visible only in direct light, spread collar, French cuffs, and a back yoke cut to allow full range of motion without pulling. The fabric is a high-thread-count synthetic-cotton blend that resists wrinkling through a twelve-hour shift and repels minor liquid contact — coffee, rain — without any active tech. Just tight weave and a surface finish applied at the mill.

The Stratum logo appears on the interior collar only — a small embossed mark. No external branding. The shirt is designed to look anonymous and expensive at the same time, which is exactly what Tier 4 professionals want. It is the default dress shirt of three separate corponation administrative dress codes, worn under suit jackets or alone with the sleeves rolled at after-hours client dinners.
what_it_says: I belong in this room and I have always belonged in this room.
story_hooks: A character receives one as a gift from a corporate contact — inside the collar, written in fading ink under the embossed logo, is a six-digit number that means nothing to them yet.

The shirt's liquid-repellent finish has an unexpected property: it also resists certain forensic chemical markers used by corponation security — someone figured this out and is selling the information.
Three men in identical Stratum poплins were seen entering a building that subsequently lost all external communications for four hours.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A pristine, structured dress shirt with an air of understated corporate authority. The silhouette is sharp and tailored without being ostentatious—it drapes cleanly from the shoulders with a subtle A-line that accommodates movement. When worn alone, the spread collar frames the neck with professional restraint; under a suit jacket, it becomes invisible scaffolding for power. The self-stripe catches light like a holographic security feature, but only when you're looking—most of the time, pure white anonymity.
physical_description.fit: Slim tailored through the torso with strategic back yoke shaping that prevents pull across the shoulders during a fourteen-hour shift at a desk or in a hover-transport. The body is cut close enough to look expensive, loose enough to move freely. Sleeves taper to the wrist without binding, designed to roll cleanly for after-hours client dinners or emergency field work.
physical_description.primary_material: High-thread-count synthetic-cotton blend poplin weave. Engineered to maintain structure without starch, resist wrinkles through extended wear, and shed minor liquid contact through mill-applied hydrophobic surface treatment—not active tech, just chemistry.
physical_description.texture: Crisp to the touch with a subtle self-stripe that creates micro-texture variation visible only in direct light. The weave is tight and uniform, with a slight sheen that reads as quality without flash. The fabric has a faint stiffness when new, softening into broken-in luxury after a handful of washes.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pristine white base with an almost-invisible self-stripe in the same white—visible only when light hits at specific angles, creating a barely-there geometric pattern that signals attention to detail. No contrasting accents or trim.
physical_description.closures: Mother-of-pearl buttons down the front placket. French cuffs with matching pearl buttons for link cufflinks (a separate purchase, a tier-signal of its own). Spread collar remains unsnapped, designed to sit open or buttoned to the throat.
distinctive_features: Back yoke cut with ergonomic shaping for unrestricted shoulder movement
French cuffs—professional but flexible, designed to roll or cuff with cufflinks
Self-stripe visible only in direct light—a quiet flex of textile engineering
Embossed Stratum logo on interior collar only—no external branding
Hydrophobic mill finish for liquid repulsion without active tech
Perfectly symmetrical button placement and stitching—zero production variance
Concealed placket stitching for seamless front appearance
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 corporate. Not Tier 1 bespoke (no custom tailoring, no rare materials), but decisively above Tier 3 functional wear. The price point is in the 450-600 Φ range—accessible to mid-level corpo administrators but still an investment. Worn as a uniform of aspiration.
physical_description.cultural_context: The shirt of someone who doesn't need to prove they're corporate—they've moved past the logo-splattered phase into the phase where anonymity and perfect execution ARE the status symbol. Worn by account managers, junior executives, compliance officers, and administrative staff who've achieved enough security to opt out of visible branding. It says: I belong in climate-controlled offices. I have access to bathrooms with real soap. I make enough to replace this if I spill coffee on it.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new or fresh from dry-cleaning; after a week of rotation, shows evidence of actual wear—slight collar creasing, minor wrinkling at the forearms if worn rolled, faint stress creases at the button holes. The hydrophobic finish means it rarely looks stained, even after minor incidents. Perfectly maintained examples look nearly identical from day one to day five hundred.
